svg.text: EACH RUNG IS A PROMISE FROM CHAPTER 02 — HERE IS WHAT IT COSTS TO KEEP

g.text: requires a retry or a hedge that succeeded — and it is
paid for out of the latency budget, not out of thin air
requires a partial flag in the contract, so the caller
can tell this answer from a complete one
requires something rebuildable to serve from, a stated
bound, and an as-of timestamp on the response
requires a handle, a deadline, and a way to reach the
client later — which is a design obligation, not a message
requires a typed error and a retry-after the caller can
actually act on. Far better than it sounds

svg.text: never a rung on any ladder, at any load, under any pressure.
If a mechanism can produce this, that is a finding, not a trade-off.
Down the ladder is worse for the caller. The last rung you are permitted to reach must still be an answer they can use.
